title: Evaluation of an innovative concept for group education, individual diagnosis and therapy planning in a university endometriosis outpatient clinic – a mixed-methods study
summary:
Endometriosis is a common chronic disease in women of reproductive age and leads to pain, infertility and a reduced quality of life. The Department of Gynecological Endocrinology and Fertility Disorders at the University Hospital Heidelberg (UKHD) has therefore developed the “Endometriosis Information Day” to help patients get a diagnosis faster and learn how to deal with the disease better. In a lecture, about 30 patients are educated about endometriosis. As part of this event, questionnaires about the disease are collected.
The aim of the presented study is to record the perceptions and evaluations of the participants regarding the process and benefits of the information day. For this purpose, an interview is conducted with about 25 patients after the endometriosis information day in order to write down and evaluate their experiences. In addition, 150 patients will be asked to evaluate the event format using a questionnaire. After 3 months, the patients will be asked to complete a follow-up questionnaire to examine any changes in their experience of the disease. 
The study is expected to be completed by fall 2025. The time required per patient is approximately 2.5 hours in total. 
The results should enable new approaches to research, as well as the transferability of the “information day” concept to other illnesses and clinics.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients attending the UFK endometriosis information day. According to the patient information on the clinic's website, the event is aimed at the following women:
“They suspect they have endometriosis and would like to be seen during our office hours for a consultation, to confirm the diagnosis and to learn about the condition.”
“They have recently been diagnosed with endometriosis and would like advice on further treatment.”
Exclusion criteria:
Patients refusing to participate in the study; missing consent; patients legally incapable of giving consent; insufficient understanding of the German language; patients under the age of 18.
